new.text:
Complete comparison: 1404 printed facsimile pp. 143, 144; 1428 edited digital presentation, vol. 1 pp. 248, 249. All stored Arabic and English paragraphs, early page boundaries, and later body and notes were read. No manuscript collation or independent human specialist certification is claimed.

All three divisions, every example, the regress objection and the author's evaluations of the alternative replies are present in Arabic and English. No original authorial note or citation is missing. The translation preserves the difference between asserting a thing's existence and attributing something to an existing subject, which supplies the metaphysical qualification of the logical presupposition rule.

Adopted: قاعدة الفرعيّه → قاعدة الفرعيّة. Restore the feminine adjective's tāʾ marbūṭa; early144 and later249 give the standard form. Grade: orthographic-alignment-with-both-witnesses.

At 1428 vol.1 p.248 n.1 the editor limits the opening divisions to common predication by comparison with the author's Bidayat al-Hikma p.132. At p.249 n.4 he quotes the author's Bidaya annotation at p.103 against allowing exceptions to rational rules. These are discussion-level cross-references: kinds of predication connect to the existential status required for attributive judgment.

Retained variant: Early144/base have بانتقاضه; later249 has بانتقاضها, changing grammatical reference to the rule rather than the preceding universality claim. Retain the transmitted base construction; the argument and English meaning are unchanged.
